pr_title: Do not throw error when we can't get canonical path
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102891

/sig storage
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon


```release-note
vSphere: Fix regression in 1.20+ during attach disk if datastore is within a storage folder or datastore cluster.
```
pr_comments:
Note to reviewers I have tested this patch with datastore present in storage folder. Before:

```
E0616 15:25:43.564057  607497 vsphere.go:942] failed to get canonical path for  on node attach.home.lan: failed to get path 
from dummy request: ServerFaultCode: Invalid datastore path '[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar/team-ssd-intel] kubevols/kube-
dummyDisk.vmdk'. is not a FileNotFound error
```

After fix:

```
I0616 15:28:54.581773  648172 reconciler.go:295] attacherDetacher.AttachVolume started for volume "pvc-43d56ecb-8bc8-42ca-
99c6-b4a3c2ecd346" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar/team-ssd-intel] 
kubevols/kubernetes-dynamic-pvc-43d56ecb-8bc8-42ca-99c6-b4a3c2ecd346.vmdk") from node "attach.home.lan" 
W0616 15:28:54.591265  648172 datacenter.go:269] QueryVirtualDiskUuid failed for diskPath: "[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar
/team-ssd-intel] kubevols/kube-dummyDisk.vmdk". err: ServerFaultCode: Invalid datastore path '[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar/team-ssd-intel] kubevols/kube-dummyDisk.vmdk'.
I0616 15:28:54.798010  648172 operation_generator.go:368] AttachVolume.Attach succeeded for volume "pvc-43d56ecb-
8bc8-42ca-99c6-b4a3c2ecd346" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar/team-ssd-intel] 
kubevols/kubernetes-dynamic-pvc-43d56ecb-8bc8-42ca-99c6-b4a3c2ecd346.vmdk") from node "attach.home.lan" 
I0616 15:28:54.798079  648172 event.go:291] "Event occurred" object="default/sandbox-5f6bcc6c9-jgwq5" kind="Pod" 
apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="SuccessfulAttachVolume" message="AttachVolume.Attach succeeded for volume \"pvc-
43d56ecb-8bc8-42ca-99c6-b4a3c2ecd346\" "

```

Note - even though QueryVirtualDiskUuid failed, the attach operation still succeeded.
Clearly a bug fix, so I'm ok on that level approving. Would be nice to see one of our vsphere experts review and lgtm before I approve.

issue_context.title: regression in vsphere attach disk call with invalid canonical path
issue_context.body:
When we introduced https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95447 we added an additional check during attach disk call to check for canonical path - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95447/files#diff-5000d45019379218cc35bc5f967f2731b4dbff230399361c8f6b9a8af3e7e1f0R928

Now this is creating a regression in many deployments because when volume is created, canonical path gets replaced - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/vsphere.go#L1467
and hence when attach is attempted k8s can't find canonical path of the volume anymore.

It throws following error:

```
E0615 19:43:13.184859  155096 attacher.go:93] Error attaching volume "[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar/team-ssd-intel] kubevols/kubernetes-dynamic-pvc-9ca3e73f-841f-49ab-95ad-7de96881f06a.vmdk" to node "attach.home.lan": failed to get path from dummy request: ServerFaultCode: Invalid datastore path '[/Datacenter/datastore/foobar/team-ssd-intel] kubevols/kube-dummyDisk.vmdk'. is not a FileNotFound error                      
```

There are two ways of fixing this. We could decide to use old `vmDiskPath` in attach code, if we can't fetch canonical path or we could decide not to replace canonical path during provisioning. 

cc @divyenpatel 

/sig storage
comments:
@gnufied: This issue is currently awaiting triage.

The code that replaces canonical Path during provisioning is pretty old and hence I don't remember/know why we are doing that. But since there could be many existing PVs that now have different canonical path - I think it might be safest to merge - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102892 to prevent any regressions.

review_comments: Does it matter what the error was? At least one of the possible errors seems to be a failure to parse the vmDiskPath. Would you still want to throw an error in that case?

Validating anything here could be a regression and hence I am leaving the error alone and using original disk path present in PV if we can't get canonical path. It is upto backend then to decide if it can attach the disk.  This still gets us the fix we wanted in original PR.
